construct: The vitelline duct normally connects the embryonic midgut to the yolk sac and involutes during early development. Incomplete obliteration can leave a true ileal diverticulum; ectopic gastric mucosa may secrete acid, ulcerating adjacent ileal mucosa and causing painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Painless pediatric lower-GI bleeding with technetium uptake synchronous with gastric mucosa identifies a Meckel diverticulum containing ectopic gastric tissue.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Urachal remnants also connect embryonic structures to the umbilicus but derive from the allantoic/bladder tract, not the ileal lesion detected by Meckel scanning.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The ileal bleeding phenotype and gastric-mucosa tracer uptake uniquely identify persistence of the vitelline duct.
